android.desc:
Bluai is your digital shield against hurricanes and tropical cyclones in Mexico. It alerts you based on your actual distance from the storm, shows you the risk in your area, and tells you what to do and where to go, even without a signal.

When a cyclone approaches, the first thing that fails is information. Bluai takes official bulletins from the National Meteorological Service and the Mexican government's SIAT-CT scale, translates them to your specific location, and guides you before, during, and after the impact.

OFFICIAL ALERTS, CALCULATED FOR YOU
You receive notifications based on the actual distance between your location and the cyclone, following the official five-level SIAT-CT scale: Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red. Each alert includes the risk level, official recommendations, and bulletin data: distance, sustained winds, gusts, and pressure. Orange and Red alerts sound even if you have quiet hours enabled.

RISK MAP OF YOUR AREA
See what's happening near you: flood and landslide zones, road closures and blockades, danger points, and aid locations such as temporary shelters, emergency shelters, and collection centers. This map shows your neighborhood, not your state.

AI-POWERED GUIDANCE, WITH OR WITHOUT INTERNET
Ask in natural language what to do and where to go. Bluai responds with clear, non-alarmist steps. With internet access, it uses cloud-based AI. Without internet, a Llama model from Meta runs directly on your phone, so it keeps responding even if the network goes down or the power goes out.

COMMUNITY REPORTS
You and your neighbors can mark what you see on the map: a flooded street, a shelter distributing food, a downed power pole. Each report shows the distance, how long ago it was posted, and whether others have confirmed it.

SOS CONTACTS
Import your contacts and build your support network in seconds. With one button, everyone receives an alert with your location.

CHAT WITHOUT NETWORK OR DATA
If cell towers go down, Bluai connects via Bluetooth to other nearby phones that also have the app, allowing you to send and receive messages without internet access.

Bluai is free and includes a risk map, official alerts, community reports, and online and offline AI guidance. Family protection features and an emergency button are part of the paid plans.

quotes.text:
Location: Mexico City, Mexico
Remote: Yes — US timezone
Willing to relocate: Yes
Technologies: Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, LangChain, RAG, pgvector,
PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, PyTorch ExecuTorch, LoRA fine-tuning, Next.js,
React Native, TypeScript, Docker
Résumé/CV: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zYNrg8UpUF1jrW3TFBJ3FST1cNvBotDz1fp0QvZ3iuk/edit?usp=sharing
Email: diego@diegocm.dev

22, self-taught. Won a $100K Meta Llama Impact Grant for Bluai and
presented it at LlamaCon on 2025

Bluai (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bluai.app&hl=en) is a hurricane early-warning app live on Google Play in Mexico,
built offline-first because during a hurricane the network is the first
thing to go. An online RAG pipeline and an on-device Llama 3.2
(ExecuTorch, NPU-accelerated) sit behind one interface, picking 1B or 3B
based on device RAM, so the UI never knows which brain answered. When
everything is down it falls back to Bluetooth/Wi-Fi mesh chat over a
multi-hop wire protocol.

Email me one paragraph about something broken or missing in
your product. I'll build a working prototype and send you the repo plus a
short video of it running, within 48 hours. Free. No call, no interview,
no invoice. If you like it, we talk. If not, you keep the code.

Flexible on compensation for the right team. I'm optimizing for who I'd
be learning from, more than thinking in numbers.
